szoveg_eredeti:
The University of Maryland, Baltimore County (UMBC) invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor position in the broad area of Artificial Intelligence (AI) for Mechanical/Chemical/Biochemical/Environmental Engineering Systems. In this context AI denotes all aspects of artificial intelligence, machine learning, and related methods.

UMBC is a nationally recognized public research university distinguished by inclusive excellence, innovative teaching, a strong commitment to student success, and research that addresses complex societal challenges. The College of Engineering and Information Technology (COEIT) seeks an innovative scholar whose research advances engineering science and technology through the development, integration, or innovative application of artificial intelligence and machine learning methods.

The successful candidate will hold a primary appointment in either the Department of Mechanical Engineering (ME) or the Department of Chemical, Biochemical, and Environmental Engineering (CBEE), based on their research and teaching interests and the strategic needs of the departments, and will join the College during a period of strategic planning and growth. They will be expected to establish an externally funded research program, contribute to undergraduate and graduate education, and foster interdisciplinary collaborations that advance engineering research through AI.

Applicants with research and teaching interests in other areas at the intersection of AI and engineering that complement the current research in the CBEE and ME Departments are also encouraged to apply, including applicants whose work has cross-disciplinary impact. UMBC seeks candidates committed to interdisciplinary research, effective teaching, mentoring students from diverse backgrounds, and embracing equity and inclusion principles in their research, teaching and service contributions.

Successful candidates will be expected to establish an externally supported research program, contribute to advances in AI-enabled engineering, teach undergraduate and graduate courses in their home department, and participate in departmental, college, and university service. Candidates must hold a PhD in mechanical engineering, chemical engineering, biochemical engineering, environmental engineering, or another closely related discipline by the appointment start date.

This is a full-time, nine-month appointment anticipated to begin in Fall 2027. The successful candidate’s primary department will be either ME or CBEE. Teaching responsibilities and workload will follow the norms of the home department.

Salary Ranges commensurate with experience.

Assistant professor: Min. $120,000 – Max. $140,000

Other components of pay are offered when necessary to meet competitive conditions.

The Department of Mechanical Engineering offers undergraduate and graduate programs integrating fundamental engineering science, computational and experimental research, and design. Faculty research spans areas including dynamics and control, robotics, fluids and thermal sciences, solid mechanics and materials, and manufacturing. More information is available at https://me.umbc.edu/.

The UMBC ABET-accredited Mechanical Engineering undergraduate program links hands-on experiences and design with theoretical, experimental, and numerical analyses. The program has over 700 enrolled undergraduate students in Fall 2026, which represents a 24% increase from the previous year. Students have opportunities for research, practical training, and internships. The department also offers M.S. and Ph.D. degrees in Mechanical Engineering. In addition to three teaching faculty, the department has 19 tenured and tenure-track faculty, leading externally funded research projects in biomechanical engineering; dynamic systems and design, including control, robotics, and autonomous systems; solid mechanics and materials science; and thermal and fluid sciences. Faculty collaborate with colleagues across UMBC, nearby institutions, and industry.

Current research in the CBEE Department (https://cbee.umbc.edu) focuses on biochemical, biomedical, bioprocess, environmental, computational, and water resources engineering. The CBEE department has approximately 250 undergraduate and 55 graduate students, 12 tenure-track faculty, and three full-time professional-track (i.e., teaching) faculty. At the undergraduate level, the department provides tracks in three areas: traditional Chemical Engineering; Biotechnology and Bioengineering; and Environmental Engineering and Sustainability. All three tracks lead to the B.S. degree in Chemical Engineering. At the graduate level, the department offers M.S. and Ph.D. degrees in Chemical and Biochemical Engineering and Environmental Engineering. Our students participate in the Meyerhoff Scholars Program, the Meyerhoff Graduate Fellows Program, and the Center for Women in Technology, which have achieved national renown for inclusive excellence through the successful training of underrepresented students for careers in academia and industry.

The UMBC community is dedicated to excellence in higher education through an inclusive culture that connects innovative teaching and learning, research across disciplines, and civic engagement. UMBC advances knowledge, economic prosperity, and social justice by welcoming and inspiring inquisitive minds from all backgrounds. UMBC is a minority-serving institution and Carnegie Classification R1 (very high research activity) public university with an enrollment of approximately 14,000 students. US News & World Report consistently ranks UMBC as a national leader in diversity, innovation, and teaching.

COEIT (https://coeit.umbc.edu/) is a collaborative environment composed of about 170 tenure-track and teaching faculty, 70 academic staff, and over 6,200 students. COEIT is advancing a strategic vision centered on Convergence Research, Inclusive Excellence, and Partnerships for Public Impact. The Dean supports innovative initiatives to tackle grand challenges in research. These efforts are reinforced by the Center for Cybersecurity, Center for Accelerated Real Time Analytics, Center for Advanced Sensor Technology, Center for Real-time Distributed Sensing and Autonomy, Center for Space Sciences and Technology, Center for Urban Environmental Research & Education, Center for Navigation, Timing & Frequency Research, Center for Research in Emergent Manufacturing, and NSF HDR Institute for Harnessing Data and Model Revolution in the Polar Regions, all of which are directed by faculty in COEIT. In addition, the College facilitates community-engaged research through the Shriver Center, which has a 30+ year record of working in Baltimore City and surrounding areas. The College supports faculty through the Eminent Scholar Mentoring Program, the Faculty Development Center, and the ADVANCE Program.

Information on the four COEIT departments is available on their websites. COEIT offers undergraduate and graduate programs in Chemical and Biochemical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Environmental Engineering, Human-Centered Computing, Information Systems, and Mechanical Engineering. COEIT faculty and research staff generated more than $23 million in research expenditures in fiscal year 2025. Many UMBC students are supported by the Meyerhoff Scholars Program, the Meyerhoff Graduate Fellows Program, and the Center for Women in Technology, which have earned national recognition for excellence through training of students from underrepresented groups for careers in academia and industry.
